The '''DecipherCon 1999 Team Event''' was a Star Wars CCG team side event at [[DecipherCon 1999]] (11–14 November 1999, Virginia Beach, Virginia). It is separate from the [[1999 Decipher World Championship]] held at the same convention. A team of four won it: [[Martin Akesson]], [[Paul Todd Feldman]], [[Koen Meijssen]] and [[Yannick Lapointe]].<ref name="trando-iv7">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026204829/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv7.htm Martin Akesson interview], [[Trandosite]] (31 August 2000)</ref><ref name="drazin">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/ErikDark.html Feldman's Drazin Deck: Decipher Con Team Play Winning Deck], Paul Todd Feldman, Torch Industries. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000303173004/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/ErikDark.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="harvest">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/Erik.html Feldman's Harvest Deck], Paul Todd Feldman, Torch Industries. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011105084834/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/Erik.html Internet Archive]</ref>

* '''Date:''' November 1999
* '''Site:''' Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Endor]]
* '''Winner:''' [[Martin Akesson]], [[Paul Todd Feldman]], [[Koen Meijssen]] and [[Yannick Lapointe]]

Feldman published both decks on [[Torch Industries]]: the Drazin deck as his "Decipher Con Team Play Winning Deck"<ref name="drazin" />, and Harvest under the heading "Regional Qualifier/DecipherCon Team Winning Deck". On Harvest he wrote:<ref name="harvest" />

<blockquote>"A version of this deck won me the Regional and the Team Event at Deciphercon."</blockquote>

The Drazin deck has [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] cards and no [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] cards, and Torch Industries first shows it on 3 March 2000, which places the event at DecipherCon 1999.

== Team ==

In a 2025 interview Feldman showed a 1999 Decipher Champ plaque from the team event. He said the team was four players and that he was the only American on it.<ref name="drtorch">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I SWCCG PDS2: DRTORCH Worlds Finalist 1996, 1997, 1999, 2000 Interview] (BillBisco2, 29 May 2025). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261014143045/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive]</ref>

On how the event ran, he said teams played against other teams, with cumulative points and differential, and that his last game decided the win:<ref name="drtorch" />

<blockquote>"I think the way they ran it is we had cumulative points as our win records and our differential as a team. ... We were just we had individual games but what we didn't play each other because we're on the we played other teams. ... I remember I had to win my game for us to win it"</blockquote>
